title: Glycerol Stock Preparation for E. coli Cultures
author: Tim Dobbs

steps.title: Prepare 50% glycerol solution
steps.instruction: Make a sterile solution containing 50 % (v/v) glycerol mixed with 50 % deionized water; keep the solution ready for dispensing.

steps.title: Label and de‑cap cryo tubes
steps.instruction: Label each cryo tube with the strain identifier and replicate number, then remove the caps from all cryo tubes and from the 50 mL conical glycerol tube (also de‑cap culture tubes if the cultures are in tubes).

steps.title: Dispense glycerol into tubes
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL of the 50 % glycerol solution to each labeled cryo tube.

steps.title: Add culture to glycerol
steps.instruction: Pipette 500 µL of each E. coli liquid culture (grown to an acceptable optical density) into the corresponding glycerol‑filled cryo tubes; change the pipette tip between different strains.

steps.title: Cap, mix, and store
steps.instruction: Recap each tube, gently vortex or flick to mix, and place the tubes in a –80 °C freezer for long‑term storage.

steps.title: Verify sample layout
steps.instruction: Confirm the total number of samples and replicates; ensure the calculated number of cryo tubes fits on the robot deck (the protocol will raise an error if too many).
